pathway.title: Trinity Industries Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The leased fleet is a dependable but short-dated anchor. Utilization is 97.0% and rents are fixed monthly for one to ten years, but the average remaining lease term is 2.7 years, the Leasing Group margin before lease portfolio sales and the divestiture gain fell 5.0 percentage points to 30.5% in nine months 2026, and management says maintenance and compliance costs remain elevated, so renewal pricing and cost control decide how steady fleet cash flow stays. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 40, 43; calculation C8; calculation C9

- Reported leverage overstates the improvement. Net debt is 5.04x EBITDA at 2026-09-30 and 5.04x pro forma for share repurchases settled in October 2026, but two non-cash gains of USD 325.8 million are 31.78% of twelve-month EBITDA and leverage without them is 7.39x, up from 6.90x at year-end 2025 on a perimeter that changed in between; the effect of the October 2026 term loan is not established. Operating profit before the TRIP Holdings gain and a facility sale gain was USD 251.5 million in nine months 2026, 19.85% below the USD 313.8 million of nine months 2025, yet 57.62% of that fall is earnings of the exited partnerships and not weaker operations. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 38–39; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C15; calculation C16

- The non-recourse structure shields the senior notes from fleet debt but leaves their cash source unmeasured. Non-recourse debt is 88.75% of the total and its pledged railcars are carried at 1.21x its amount, so the recourse claim is USD 598.9 million of 7.75% senior notes due 2028, about USD 46.5 million of coupon a year; how much cash reaches the parent after fleet debt service is not stated, so corporate creditors depend on a residual they cannot measure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C5

- Cash flow after fleet investment is volatile and distributions absorb nearly all of it. It was negative USD 28.7 million in FY2025 and negative USD 32.8 million in nine months 2026, and positive USD 165.5 million over twelve months only because nine months 2025 was weaker; distributions of USD 153.9 million over the same twelve months left USD 11.6 million, and wholly-owned non-recourse debt rose USD 152.7 million in nine months 2026. Management guides 2026 net fleet investment of USD 300 million to USD 350 million, which implies USD 59.2 million to USD 109.2 million in the fourth quarter. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 49, 51; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14

- Manufacturing has stabilized at a lower level but stays cyclical, concentrated and exposed to Mexico duties. Deliveries fell 45.93% in FY2025 and the segment's operating profit 60.77%, but orders in nine months 2026 were 0.97x deliveries against 0.54x in FY2025 and backlog of USD 1,646.7 million is 0.90% below year-end. One customer is roughly 43% of manufacturing revenue, most railcars are built in Mexico, and a petition alleges dumping margins of 12.70% to 32.58% with no accrual recorded. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 48, 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 45–46; calculation C20; calculation C18; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24

- Refinancing pressure has moved from 2026 to 2027 and 2028, at a higher cost. Redemptions and the Tribute Rail deconsolidation addressed 84.78% of the USD 1,096.1 million scheduled for 2026 at year-end, but notes at 3.82% were replaced with notes at 5.36% and notes at 3.10% with a loan at SOFR plus 1.30%, and USD 2,360.2 million, 43.18% of year-end principal, falls due in 2027 and 2028. Committed liquidity fell 19.57% to USD 897.2 million, 80.16% of the fall coming from lower warehouse availability. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23, 35, 47; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C29

- Financial policy is a moderate risk. No controlling holder is identified, and the issuer reports revolver covenant ratios of 0.75x net leverage against a 3.75x maximum and 13.13x coverage against a 2.25x minimum, but both are defined for a restricted perimeter that is not reconciled to consolidated debt, buybacks of USD 54.4 million over twelve months continue and USD 114.4 million of authorization remains. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 49–51; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C30; calculation C11; calculation C37

runs.text: Contracted, highly utilized fleet cash flow is the first strength. Utilization of 97.0% and fixed rents of one to ten years give rent visibility, and the cash goes first to secured notes with no recourse to Trinity, so a fleet shortfall is contained and the senior notes are not asked to fund it. This lowers the probability that fleet stress reaches the corporate creditor. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 43; calculation C8; calculation C4

Collateral and ring-fencing are the second strength. Pledged railcars at book value cover non-recourse debt 1.21x, and USD 798.8 million of equipment is unpledged and supports warehouse availability, so fleet lenders are well protected on book values and the unpledged pool is a source of liquidity. Market values and recovery are outside this assessment. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation C6

Demonstrated market access is the third. The issuer placed USD 480.8 million of notes in April 2026 at 5.36%, arranged a USD 349.8 million term loan in October 2026 and amended its USD 600.0 million revolver to mature on 2031-06-12, or on 2028-04-15 if the senior notes due 2028 are not repaid, so the issuer reports completing the refinancing of its 2026 maturities, which supports the near-term refinancing view at a higher cost. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23, 35, 47; calculation C26; calculation C25

Vertical integration and order recovery are the fourth. Substantially all leased railcars are built by the Rail Products Group, orders were 0.97x deliveries in nine months 2026, and about 25% of backlog value is due in the fourth quarter of 2026 and 50% in 2027, which gives the manufacturing arm visible volume for the next year. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; calculation C21; calculation C22

Reported leverage that depends on gains is the first weakness. Two non-cash gains of USD 325.8 million are 31.78% of twelve-month EBITDA, so the reported improvement to 5.04x is partly accounting for exits, and leverage without them is 7.39x; creditors should size debt service capacity on the lower earnings base. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

A short remaining lease term with a falling margin is the second. The 2.7-year average remaining term means rents reprice within a few years while maintenance and compliance costs are elevated, so a softer rental market would reach cash flow quickly and the 5.0 percentage point fall in the Leasing Group margin may continue. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 40, 43; calculation C8; calculation C9

Distributions and fleet growth funded by borrowing are the third. Cash flow after fleet investment was negative in FY2025 and in nine months 2026 while distributions of USD 170.0 million and USD 117.4 million were paid, and wholly-owned non-recourse debt rose USD 152.7 million, so debt does not fall with fleet amortization and the corporate buffer stays thin. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 49; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C13

Cyclical, concentrated manufacturing with Mexico duty exposure is the fourth. Manufacturing is 44.14% of revenue, deliveries fell 45.93% in FY2025, one customer is roughly 43% of manufacturing revenue and most railcars are built in Mexico, so an order pause or duty would cut volume or margin in the segment that supports corporate cash flow; Mexican long-lived assets are only USD 94.3 million, so the exposure is cost and volume and not asset impairment. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C23; calculation C24

Refinancing step-up and shrinking warehouse headroom are the fifth. Notes at 3.82% and 3.10% have been replaced at 5.36% and SOFR plus 1.30%, USD 2,360.2 million of year-end principal is due in 2027 and 2028, and committed liquidity fell 19.57%, mostly because warehouse availability depends on eligible unpledged railcars and fell, so interest cost rises and execution risk sits in 2027. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23, 47; calculation C25; calculation C27; calculation C29

runs.text: In April 2026 a limited-purpose leasing subsidiary issued USD 480.8 million of Series 2026-1 secured railcar notes, USD 447.4 million at a fixed 5.35% and USD 33.4 million at a fixed 5.56%, with a stated final maturity of April 19, 2056; the notes are non-recourse to Trinity and the proceeds redeemed the Series 2019-1 notes, of which USD 377.1 million was outstanding at a 3.82% rate. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22

On April 9, 2026 the leasing subsidiary TILC agreed to contribute its 42.56% interest in TRIP Holdings and a 0.2% interest in Triumph Rail Holdings to NP SPE Holdings LP, a Napier Park vehicle, for an 11.2% limited partnership interest, valued at USD 112.9 million. The exchange was completed in April 2026, deconsolidated TRIP Holdings and its Tribute Rail debt of USD 270.6 million, and produced a non-cash pre-tax gain of USD 131.6 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 36

In June 2026 Trinity amended and restated its USD 600.0 million unsecured revolving credit facility, extending maturity to the earlier of June 12, 2031 or April 15, 2028 if the senior notes due 2028 have not been repaid, adding an option to increase commitments by up to USD 300.0 million subject to customary conditions and modifying the leverage ratio calculation for certain cash balances. In the same month it acquired a 32.0% interest in an Indian railcar lessor for USD 37.6 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19, 21

On October 19, 2026, after the September 30 balance sheet, a limited-purpose subsidiary entered into a USD 349.8 million non-recourse term loan at daily simple SOFR plus 1.30% maturing October 19, 2031, and used the proceeds to redeem USD 280.9 million of Series 2019-2 notes at a 3.10% rate and to repay warehouse borrowings; an interest rate swap was added in October 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23

Earlier, in December 2025, TILC exchanged its interest in Triumph for Napier Park's interest in RIV 2013, giving it full ownership of RIV 2013 and a non-cash pre-tax gain of USD 194.2 million, and in October 2025 a subsidiary issued USD 535.2 million of Series 2025-1 notes that redeemed older notes and repaid warehouse borrowings. In April 2025 the TRL-2023 term loan was increased to USD 1.05 billion and extended to April 30, 2030. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 94, 104–105

fields.value: Financial foundation for Trinity Industries Inc (issuer trn-99780), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the five supplied filings, in US dollars. Net debt and leverage use balance-sheet carrying values and a reported EBITDA derived from printed lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported net debt to EBITDA fell from 7.95x in FY2023 to 5.04x over the twelve months to 2026-09-30, but two non-cash divestiture gains inflate that EBITDA; without them it is 7.39x, so creditors should read leverage as about seven times and no longer improving.

fields.value: Debt is USD 5,325.0 million at 2026-09-30, of which USD 4,726.1 million is non-recourse fleet debt secured on railcars, against cash of USD 158.3 million. Cash interest paid is not printed for 2026, so cover is stated only to FY2025 at 3.50x; an interest expense proxy gives 3.85x for the latest twelve months. Committed liquidity fell to USD 897.2 million from USD 1,115.5 million at year-end as warehouse availability dropped to USD 146.5 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has improved on the reported measure but not on the underlying one. Net debt of USD 5,166.7 million over reported EBITDA of USD 1,025.2 million gives 5.04x, against 5.49x at FY2025 and 7.95x at FY2023. Gains of USD 194.2 million in Q4 2025 and USD 131.6 million in Q2 2026, both non-cash gains from moving railcar partnerships out of the consolidated statements, sit inside that EBITDA; removing them leaves USD 699.4 million and a ratio of 7.39x, an Analyst Judgement adjustment shown beside the reported figure. Because the earnings of those partnerships are in the twelve-month figure while their debt has left the balance sheet, even the reported ratio is flattered by a perimeter mismatch that the filings do not quantify.

fields.value: Interest cover is modest and cannot be stated on a cash basis for the latest period. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 3.50x in FY2025 and 2.89x in FY2024. For the twelve months to 2026-09-30 only interest expense, net of USD 266.1 million is available, which gives a proxy cover of 3.85x, or 2.63x without the two gains. Creditors cannot confirm the cash figure until the filings print it.

fields.value: Data quality and definition risks matter to how far these ratios can be trusted. The issuer reports no EBITDA, so reported EBITDA here is total operating profit plus depreciation and amortization, and it includes disposition gains of USD 290.8 million in FY2025. The issuer reports a covenant net leverage ratio of 0.75x at 2026-09-30 against 5.04x on the consolidated basis used here, because its covenant perimeter and definition are not supplied; the two are not reconciled. A printed dash is treated as not supplied rather than zero.

fields.value: Subsequent events after 2026-09-30 are kept out of the period figures. A USD 349.8 million non-recourse term loan on 2026-10-19 funded the redemption of USD 280.9 million of 2019 notes and the repayment of warehouse borrowings, so its effect on net debt is not established; the cash settlement of USD 1.3 million of share repurchases moves pro forma net debt to USD 5,168.0 million, still 5.04x. Supplier finance of USD 46.3 million, down from USD 49.1 million at year-end, sits inside accounts payable and is working-capital float rather than debt.

fields.value: Business, ownership and transaction facts for Trinity Industries Inc (issuer trn-99780), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer, its owners and control, operating model, transactions and governance behaviour from the five supplied filings, read for creditors. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trinity is a listed North American railcar lessor and manufacturer with no controlling owner disclosed, so creditors rely on lease-fleet cash flow that mostly services non-recourse debt, while a shrinking manufacturing arm and two partnership restructurings make the reporting perimeter unstable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The lease fleet was 97.0% utilized at 2026-09-30 with an average remaining lease term of 2.7 years, and non-recourse debt is 88.75% of consolidated debt, but manufacturing fell from 62.95% of revenue in FY2024 to 44.14% in FY2025 and one customer supplied 19% of FY2025 revenue. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium on documented behaviour, because shareholder returns continued while cash flow after fleet investment was negative, and the proxy statement and executed financing documents are not supplied.

fields.value: - No controlling owner is identified, so governance risk cannot be read from sponsor identity and none is inferred. The filings name no holder or sponsor with control, and the proxy statement that would list principal holders, board rights and related-party dealings is not supplied, so ownership conclusions stop at the listed-company facts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Leasing Group is the earnings core and its revenue base is short-dated. Rentals are fixed monthly for one to ten years, utilization is 97.0%, and the average remaining term of 2.7 years means renewals reprice the fleet within a few years; management attributes offsetting support to higher lease rates and net fleet additions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Perimeter changes, not operations alone, explain the fall in lease revenue. Leasing and management revenue fell 8.96% in nine months 2026, and the issuer attributes USD 85.1 million of the reduction to the two divested partnerships; on that reading revenue excluding them rose about USD 23.8 million, an Analyst Interpretation that the filings do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Manufacturing is cyclical, concentrated and exposed to Mexico trade action. Deliveries fell 45.93% in FY2025 and 15.03% in nine months 2026, one customer supplied 19% of FY2025 revenue, more than half of employees work in Mexico, and a petition filed on 2026-09-30 seeks antidumping and countervailing duties on tank cars imported from Mexico; the backlog of USD 1,646.7 million is 6.56% lower than a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is mixed rather than adverse. Dividends and buybacks totalled USD 170.0 million in FY2025 and USD 117.4 million in nine months 2026 while cash flow after fleet investment was negative USD 28.7 million and negative USD 32.8 million, yet no exchange, waiver, priming or related-party extraction was found and the non-recourse notes are ring-fenced from Trinity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is the stability of the leased fleet: utilization has stayed at or near 97.0%, rentals are fixed under multi-year contracts, the lessor debt is amortizing, secured on the railcars and non-recourse to Trinity, and the Leasing Group backlog of USD 333.7 million is described as fully supported by lease commitments with external customers. The annual statements carry an unqualified audit opinion, and the board is described by the company as having an independent chairman, which is management language, not a tested fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would soften if the proxy statement showed no dominant holder and no related-party fees, if the credit agreement and indenture showed tight restricted-payment limits, if the Mexico duty petition were dismissed, and if interim reports began to print cash interest and a current maturity ladder. It would harden if shareholder returns continued to exceed cash flow after fleet investment, if the single large manufacturing customer reduced orders, or if further partnership exchanges moved more debt and earnings off the consolidated statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the ownership register and governance register stop at the listed-company facts and the Medium governance level could move either way once principal holders, board rights and related-party fees are known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, investments and asset transfers is not established and the conclusion on financial policy rests on documented behaviour alone, which cannot separate willingness from capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lessee concentration in the lease book is not disclosed, only one manufacturing customer, so the durability of lease revenue cannot be tested by counterparty and the view that leasing is stable rests on utilization and lease terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earnings effect of the two partnership exits is quantified only for revenue, so comparisons of operating profit and mix across FY2024, FY2025 and nine months 2026 are not like-for-like and the shrinking-manufacturing finding is stated on reported figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No earnings release, lender presentation or current report is supplied, so events between 2026-10-29 and the 2026-11-18 cutoff are not established and the transaction list may be incomplete.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Trinity presents Medium sponsor and governance risk on the evidence supplied. The supported behaviour is continued dividends and buybacks while cash flow after fleet investment was negative, which matters because net borrowing absorbs the shortfall and keeps debt from falling; no priming, exchange, waiver or related-party extraction was found, and the lessor debt is non-recourse. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indenture. The governance review is complete with limitations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On April 9, 2026 the leasing subsidiary TILC agreed to contribute its 42.56% interest in TRIP Holdings and a 0.2% interest in Triumph Rail Holdings to NP SPE Holdings LP, a Napier Park vehicle, for an 11.2% limited partnership interest, valued at USD 112.9 million. The exchange was completed in April 2026, deconsolidated TRIP Holdings and its Tribute Rail debt of USD 270.6 million, and produced a non-cash pre-tax gain of USD 131.6 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In June 2026 Trinity amended and restated its USD 600.0 million unsecured revolving credit facility, extending maturity to the earlier of June 12, 2031 or April 15, 2028 if the senior notes due 2028 have not been repaid, adding an option to increase commitments by up to USD 300.0 million subject to customary conditions and modifying the leverage ratio calculation for certain cash balances. In the same month it acquired a 32.0% interest in an Indian railcar lessor for USD 37.6 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On October 19, 2026, after the September 30 balance sheet, a limited-purpose subsidiary entered into a USD 349.8 million non-recourse term loan at daily simple SOFR plus 1.30% maturing October 19, 2031, and used the proceeds to redeem USD 280.9 million of Series 2019-2 notes at a 3.10% rate and to repay warehouse borrowings; an interest rate swap was added in October 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier, in December 2025, TILC exchanged its interest in Triumph for Napier Park's interest in RIV 2013, giving it full ownership of RIV 2013 and a non-cash pre-tax gain of USD 194.2 million, and in October 2025 a subsidiary issued USD 535.2 million of Series 2025-1 notes that redeemed older notes and repaid warehouse borrowings. In April 2025 the TRL-2023 term loan was increased to USD 1.05 billion and extended to April 30, 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Trinity Industries Inc (issuer trn-99780), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is business quality, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring triggers from the five supplied filings and the three earlier analyses, in US dollars. No rating, relative-value, covenant-capacity or recovery conclusion is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trinity is an adequate credit: fixed-rent railcar leases service mostly non-recourse debt, but leverage above seven times underlying EBITDA, a manufacturing arm that has halved and distributions that absorb most spare cash leave corporate creditors dependent on residual cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C19; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt is 5.04x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 and 5.04x pro forma, with net debt of USD 5,168.0 million, after share repurchases settled in October 2026; without two non-cash divestiture gains it is 7.39x. The effect of the October 2026 term loan on net debt is not established. Non-recourse debt is 88.75% of the total, and pledged railcars at book value are 1.21x that debt. Over twelve months, cash flow after fleet investment of USD 165.5 million exceeded distributions of USD 153.9 million by USD 11.6 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 20, 49; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The leased fleet is a dependable but short-dated anchor. Utilization is 97.0% and rents are fixed monthly for one to ten years, but the average remaining lease term is 2.7 years, the Leasing Group margin before lease portfolio sales and the divestiture gain fell 5.0 percentage points to 30.5% in nine months 2026, and management says maintenance and compliance costs remain elevated, so renewal pricing and cost control decide how steady fleet cash flow stays.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 40, 43; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported leverage overstates the improvement. Net debt is 5.04x EBITDA at 2026-09-30 and 5.04x pro forma for share repurchases settled in October 2026, but two non-cash gains of USD 325.8 million are 31.78% of twelve-month EBITDA and leverage without them is 7.39x, up from 6.90x at year-end 2025 on a perimeter that changed in between; the effect of the October 2026 term loan is not established. Operating profit before the TRIP Holdings gain and a facility sale gain was USD 251.5 million in nine months 2026, 19.85% below the USD 313.8 million of nine months 2025, yet 57.62% of that fall is earnings of the exited partnerships and not weaker operations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 38–39; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The non-recourse structure shields the senior notes from fleet debt but leaves their cash source unmeasured. Non-recourse debt is 88.75% of the total and its pledged railcars are carried at 1.21x its amount, so the recourse claim is USD 598.9 million of 7.75% senior notes due 2028, about USD 46.5 million of coupon a year; how much cash reaches the parent after fleet debt service is not stated, so corporate creditors depend on a residual they cannot measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow after fleet investment is volatile and distributions absorb nearly all of it. It was negative USD 28.7 million in FY2025 and negative USD 32.8 million in nine months 2026, and positive USD 165.5 million over twelve months only because nine months 2025 was weaker; distributions of USD 153.9 million over the same twelve months left USD 11.6 million, and wholly-owned non-recourse debt rose USD 152.7 million in nine months 2026. Management guides 2026 net fleet investment of USD 300 million to USD 350 million, which implies USD 59.2 million to USD 109.2 million in the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 49, 51; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Manufacturing has stabilized at a lower level but stays cyclical, concentrated and exposed to Mexico duties. Deliveries fell 45.93% in FY2025 and the segment's operating profit 60.77%, but orders in nine months 2026 were 0.97x deliveries against 0.54x in FY2025 and backlog of USD 1,646.7 million is 0.90% below year-end. One customer is roughly 43% of manufacturing revenue, most railcars are built in Mexico, and a petition alleges dumping margins of 12.70% to 32.58% with no accrual recorded.

fields.value: - Refinancing pressure has moved from 2026 to 2027 and 2028, at a higher cost. Redemptions and the Tribute Rail deconsolidation addressed 84.78% of the USD 1,096.1 million scheduled for 2026 at year-end, but notes at 3.82% were replaced with notes at 5.36% and notes at 3.10% with a loan at SOFR plus 1.30%, and USD 2,360.2 million, 43.18% of year-end principal, falls due in 2027 and 2028. Committed liquidity fell 19.57% to USD 897.2 million, 80.16% of the fall coming from lower warehouse availability.

fields.value: - Financial policy is a moderate risk. No controlling holder is identified, and the issuer reports revolver covenant ratios of 0.75x net leverage against a 3.75x maximum and 13.13x coverage against a 2.25x minimum, but both are defined for a restricted perimeter that is not reconciled to consolidated debt, buybacks of USD 54.4 million over twelve months continue and USD 114.4 million of authorization remains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is asset and contract quality. Pledged railcars are carried at 1.21x the non-recourse debt they secure, utilization is 97.0%, Leasing Group orders in backlog of USD 333.7 million are fully supported by external lease commitments, orders recovered to 0.97x deliveries, the issuer reports covenant compliance with large cushions on its own definitions, and it placed USD 480.8 million of notes with a final maturity in 2056 in April 2026 and a USD 349.8 million term loan in October 2026, so market access is shown by transactions and not assumed. Cash flow after fleet investment also exceeded distributions over twelve months.

fields.value: The view would improve if the filings print cash interest paid and a current maturity ladder that confirm the 2027 and 2028 refinancing, if the Mexico petition fails at the preliminary stage, if EBITDA without gains grows while debt falls, and if the proxy statement shows no dominant holder. It would worsen if the warehouse revolving period ends on 2027-03-15 without extension, if distributions again exceed cash flow after fleet investment, if duties are imposed, or if utilization falls from 97.0% while the remaining lease term shortens further.

fields.value: Contracted, highly utilized fleet cash flow is the first strength. Utilization of 97.0% and fixed rents of one to ten years give rent visibility, and the cash goes first to secured notes with no recourse to Trinity, so a fleet shortfall is contained and the senior notes are not asked to fund it. This lowers the probability that fleet stress reaches the corporate creditor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Collateral and ring-fencing are the second strength. Pledged railcars at book value cover non-recourse debt 1.21x, and USD 798.8 million of equipment is unpledged and supports warehouse availability, so fleet lenders are well protected on book values and the unpledged pool is a source of liquidity. Market values and recovery are outside this assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demonstrated market access is the third. The issuer placed USD 480.8 million of notes in April 2026 at 5.36%, arranged a USD 349.8 million term loan in October 2026 and amended its USD 600.0 million revolver to mature on 2031-06-12, or on 2028-04-15 if the senior notes due 2028 are not repaid, so the issuer reports completing the refinancing of its 2026 maturities, which supports the near-term refinancing view at a higher cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23, 35, 47; calculation C26; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Vertical integration and order recovery are the fourth. Substantially all leased railcars are built by the Rail Products Group, orders were 0.97x deliveries in nine months 2026, and about 25% of backlog value is due in the fourth quarter of 2026 and 50% in 2027, which gives the manufacturing arm visible volume for the next year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; calculation C21; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage that depends on gains is the first weakness. Two non-cash gains of USD 325.8 million are 31.78% of twelve-month EBITDA, so the reported improvement to 5.04x is partly accounting for exits, and leverage without them is 7.39x; creditors should size debt service capacity on the lower earnings base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A short remaining lease term with a falling margin is the second. The 2.7-year average remaining term means rents reprice within a few years while maintenance and compliance costs are elevated, so a softer rental market would reach cash flow quickly and the 5.0 percentage point fall in the Leasing Group margin may continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 40, 43; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Distributions and fleet growth funded by borrowing are the third. Cash flow after fleet investment was negative in FY2025 and in nine months 2026 while distributions of USD 170.0 million and USD 117.4 million were paid, and wholly-owned non-recourse debt rose USD 152.7 million, so debt does not fall with fleet amortization and the corporate buffer stays thin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 49; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cyclical, concentrated manufacturing with Mexico duty exposure is the fourth. Manufacturing is 44.14% of revenue, deliveries fell 45.93% in FY2025, one customer is roughly 43% of manufacturing revenue and most railcars are built in Mexico, so an order pause or duty would cut volume or margin in the segment that supports corporate cash flow; Mexican long-lived assets are only USD 94.3 million, so the exposure is cost and volume and not asset impairment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C23; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing step-up and shrinking warehouse headroom are the fifth. Notes at 3.82% and 3.10% have been replaced at 5.36% and SOFR plus 1.30%, USD 2,360.2 million of year-end principal is due in 2027 and 2028, and committed liquidity fell 19.57%, mostly because warehouse availability depends on eligible unpledged railcars and fell, so interest cost rises and execution risk sits in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23, 47; calculation C25; calculation C27; calculation C29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trinity is a North American railcar lessor and manufacturer, and the leasing business is what supports debt service. The Leasing Group earns full-service operating lease rents from railroads and industrial shippers across refined products, chemicals, energy, agriculture, construction, metals and consumer products, and leasing and services provided 55.86% of FY2025 revenue; the Rail Products Group builds substantially all the leased railcars and manufacturing provided 44.14%, after manufacturing revenue fell 50.88% in FY2025. Steady rents support cash-flow visibility and secured refinancing, while manufacturing swings volume and margin and adds a concentration in one customer, so the two halves of the business carry very different credit weight.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 66; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19; calculation C36; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling holder or sponsor is identified, and ownership conclusions stop at listed-company facts because the proxy statement is not supplied. Group structure matters more than ownership: TILC holds the fleet through limited-purpose subsidiaries whose notes are non-recourse to Trinity, two partnerships were exchanged out of the consolidated group in December 2025 and April 2026, and investor-owned railcars are 34.09% of railcars under management, so servicing and fee income continue while debt left the balance sheet. The earlier governance review rated sponsor and financial-policy risk Medium, which this assessment keeps, because distributions continued while cash flow after fleet investment was negative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 43; calculation C36; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leasing revenue is predictable and contract-based, while manufacturing revenue is cyclical, discretionary and concentrated. Leasing and management revenue fell 8.96% in nine months 2026, but excluding the divested partnerships it rose USD 23.8 million, or 3.97%, so the base fleet grew with higher lease rates and net additions. Deliveries fell 45.93% in FY2025 and 15.03% in nine months 2026, orders recovered to 0.97x deliveries, and one customer is roughly 43% of manufacturing revenue, so manufacturing revenue visibility rests on a backlog of USD 1,646.7 million that is stable since year-end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 40, 45–46; calculation C33; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are not secure in either segment. The Leasing Group margin before lease portfolio sales and the divestiture gain was 30.5% in nine months 2026 against 35.5% a year earlier, with higher fleet operating costs and administrative expense up 8.5%, while the Rail Products Group margin was 7.79% in FY2024, 5.23% in FY2025 and 6.26% in nine months 2026 and its operating profit fell 60.77% in FY2025, which shows heavy operating leverage to volume. Steel and component cost is managed through contract-specific purchasing and price escalation clauses, but some materials come from a limited number of suppliers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 38, 40, 44; calculation C9; calculation C18; calculation C34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings convert to cash well below the reported EBITDA. Operating cash flow from continuing operations was 60.39% of EBITDA without gains over twelve months, after interest, and fleet investment then absorbs more: lease fleet investment is mostly new railcar additions, conversions and modifications and is partly funded by lease portfolio sales and secured debt, so cash flow after net fleet investment was USD -19.3 million in FY2023, USD 353.1 million in FY2024, USD -28.7 million in FY2025 and USD -32.8 million in nine months 2026. Fleet investment is the main discretionary lever, but maintenance and compliance spending is not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 34, 49; calculation C35; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry, buyers and suppliers matter most. Trinity competes with five major railcar lessors and four major railcar manufacturers in a market the filing calls intensely competitive, so pricing power is limited and competition rests on quality, price and service; buyers are railroads, lessors and shippers, and one manufacturing customer is roughly 43% of manufacturing revenue, so buyer power is real in manufacturing; certain materials come from a limited number of suppliers, which exposes delivery schedules and margins. New entrants and substitutes are not established from the filings as credit drivers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and economic factors are material and social and technological factors are not primary drivers. The petition seeking antidumping and countervailing duties on tank cars imported from Mexico, the Section 232 tariffs and the administration of trade policy in the United States and Mexico bear directly on a manufacturing base where most railcars are built in Mexico, and the filing says uncertainty rose in 2026; demand follows industrial production, interest rates and customer credit, and skilled-labor shortages raise cost, but social and technological factors are smaller than the trade risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the recovery in orders, higher lease rates on a utilized fleet and fee income from investor-owned railcars, which are 34.09% of railcars under management. Threats that could weaken it are the duty proceedings, cost reset on maturing low-coupon notes, softer rental markets as leases roll over within 2.7 years, and a repeat of the FY2025 delivery collapse of 45.93%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 43, 45–46; calculation C36; calculation C8; calculation C21; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is Strong, competitive advantage is Average and business diversification is Average. Trinity manages a large railcar fleet, leases it on fixed rents and builds most of its own cars, which gives scale and an integrated platform, but it names no market share, competition is intense and the business is North American with one concentrated manufacturing customer, so these dimensions support the credit without being a moat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility is Average, margin stability is Average and free cash flow stability is Weak. Growth fleet investment and distributions can be cut, but maintenance and compliance costs cannot, margins fell in leasing and moved widely in manufacturing, and cash flow after net fleet investment swung from USD 353.1 million in FY2024 to USD -28.7 million in FY2025, which makes cash available for debt reduction unreliable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 40; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C9; calculation C18; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ability to refinance is Average, liquidity position is Average and financial policy and governance is Average. Market access was shown in 2026 and the revolver runs to 2031-06-12 or 2028-04-15 if the senior notes are not repaid, but coupons rose, committed liquidity of USD 897.2 million fell 19.57% and relies in part on eligible unpledged railcars, and distributions continue while cash flow after fleet investment is thin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23, 47; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C25; calculation C29; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are the contracted fleet, ring-fenced collateralized funding and demonstrated access; the main constraints are gain-inflated leverage, thin cash after distributions and a concentrated manufacturing arm. The trend is mixed: reported net leverage improved from 7.95x in FY2023 to 5.49x in FY2025, yet leverage without gains rose from 6.90x to 7.39x on a changed perimeter. Interest cover was 3.50x on cash interest in FY2025, 3.85x on interest expense for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and 2.63x without gains, so cover is modest. The datapoints missing for a firmer view are 2026 cash interest, a current maturity ladder, parent-only cash flow, lease expiries by year, peer and rating inputs, and the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and capital structure differ from a typical leveraged borrower because most debt is secured, amortizing and non-recourse, and the borrower is also a manufacturer; no peer data is supplied, so a ranking against other railcar lessors or leveraged issuers is not established. Debt to total capitalization is 82.48%, which shows a thin equity layer behind a book-collateralized fleet. Variable-rate debt was 28% of total debt before hedges and 13% after at year-end 2025, and one percentage point higher average rates in 2026 would add USD 7.4 million of interest, so rate sensitivity is limited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 53; calculation C7; calculation C32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two earlier statements are corrected here. Financial foundation said the filings do not quantify the perimeter mismatch from the exited partnerships, and Business & governance said the earnings effect of the exits is quantified for revenue only. The quarterly report in fact states that the two divested leasing subsidiaries contributed USD 13.9 million of operating profit in the third quarter of 2025 and USD 35.9 million in nine months 2025, besides USD 85.1 million lower revenue in nine months 2026. The annual report also shows year-end debt for them, USD 469.4 million of Triumph notes at 2024-12-31 and USD 270.6 million of Tribute Rail debt at 2025-12-31. It states no interest, EBITDA or cash flow for them, and their earnings inside the twelve months to 2026-09-30 are not established, so the leverage figures stand, but the size of the earnings side is now bounded: 57.62% of the USD 62.3 million underlying fall in operating profit is the exited partnerships.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 98; calculation C17; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 months to 24 months the order book and the refinancing calendar decide the credit. Management expects about 25% of backlog value to be delivered in the fourth quarter of 2026 and 50% in 2027, net fleet investment of USD 300 million to USD 350 million in 2026, and operating capital expenditure of USD 55 million to USD 65 million; tailwinds are higher lease rates, net fleet additions and recovered orders, while headwinds are the pending Commerce decision and preliminary ITC investigation on Mexican tank cars, elevated maintenance cost, the warehouse revolving end on 2027-03-15, and replacement of low-coupon notes at higher cost. These support revenue visibility in 2027 but pressure margin and refinancing confidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 38, 45–46, 51; calculation C22; calculation C14; calculation C28; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years, lease repricing and the ladder dominate. The 2.7-year average remaining term means much of the book reprices within the period, a fleet average age of 14.8 years, up from 14.3 years, may add to maintenance cost and obsolescence exposure, and the year-end ladder shows USD 259.0 million due in 2029, USD 938.0 million in 2030 and USD 813.2 million thereafter beyond the 2027 and 2028 amounts, with the revolver at 2031-06-12, so deleveraging depends on rents holding up and on distributions staying below cash flow after fleet investment. The railcar industry has had sharp cyclical downturns with minimal backlog, and the filing states that industry order volumes and backlog are currently reduced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19, 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 43; calculation C8; calculation C27; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with a duty on Mexican tank cars or an order pause in a weak freight cycle, which breaks first in the Rail Products Group because most railcars are built in Mexico and one customer is roughly 43% of manufacturing revenue. A repeat of the FY2025 pattern, when deliveries fell 45.93% and segment operating profit fell 60.77%, would cut operating cash flow and reduce railcar sales to the Leasing Group; in a weak freight cycle the secondary market behind lease portfolio sale proceeds of USD 168.7 million in nine months 2026 would also soften, so cash flow after net fleet investment, already thin after distributions, would turn negative, net borrowing would rise and leverage without gains would stay above seven times.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19, 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 28, 46; calculation C20; calculation C18; calculation C23; calculation C12; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and refinancing would absorb the shock if management acts. The levers are suspending buybacks and dividends, which were USD 153.9 million over twelve months, cutting growth fleet investment guided at USD 300 million to USD 350 million, and drawing the revolver of USD 592.4 million; the exposure is the warehouse, whose availability depends on eligible unpledged railcars and whose revolving period ends on 2027-03-15, and the senior notes due 2028 with the revolver maturity tied to them. On stated liquidity of USD 897.2 million resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over the next 12 months, because fleet debt is non-recourse and the levers are large relative to cash flow; if the warehouse is not extended, its undrawn availability ends on 2027-03-15 and the drawn balance falls due by 2028-03-15, which would test corporate liquidity if capital markets were closed at the same time. No stress amount is stated because the filings give no basis for one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_trn.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_trn.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 47, 51; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C29; calculation C28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Trinity presents an adequate business profile supported by a 97.0% utilized, fixed-rent lease fleet, ring-fenced non-recourse funding with 1.21x book collateral cover and demonstrated market access, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 7.39x without gains, a 2.7-year average remaining lease term and distributions that absorb 92.99% of cash flow after fleet investment. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at fleet level and weak after growth investment and distributions. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the warehouse before 2027-03-15, addressing the senior notes due 2028 and holding market access at current coupons, and on the net debt effect of the October 2026 term loan, which is not established. The primary downside path is a duty or order pause in manufacturing that reduces cash flow while distributions continue and net borrowing rises. Further analysis would require parent-only cash flow, current cash interest, a current maturity ladder, lease expiries by year, and the executed credit agreement and proxy statement. Top risk: rising secured debt funding distributions and growth against a gain-inflated earnings base.
